clue.text: Style of plain title girl received

indicators.note: a title that has received a girl holds her name inside it

parts.note: Mr is the plain everyday title for a man, abbreviated MR
Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A posh-looking style name for a modest gentleman with a young woman on his arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A manner is a way or style of doing something, as in 'in the grand manner'.

clue.text: Knock into the air and begin to play

definitions.meaning: to hit something upwards, as a ball struck skywards
a band strikes up a tune when it starts playing

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both hitting something upward and a band launching into music.

clue.text: These London companies providing current to railway

parts.note: a live wire is one carrying electric current

explanation.surface: London firms that supply electricity to the rail network.
explanation.walkthrough: The livery companies are the ancient trade guilds of the City of London, such as the Goldsmiths and the Fishmongers.
explanation.definitionFit: The City of London's old trade guilds are collectively called its livery companies.

indicators.note: an amendment made to the word redoing alters the order of its letters

explanation.surface: A proposed amendment to redo something was simply brushed aside.
explanation.definitionFit: To disregard something is to take no notice of it, the same as overlooking it.

clue.text: In plate, an accompaniment to coffee

indicators.note: the clue places the word an within the plate, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a dish is a plate

explanation.surface: Something served on a plate alongside a cup of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: A Danish is a sweet pastry, short for Danish pastry, often eaten with coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A Danish pastry is a classic sweet snack served with a morning coffee.

parts.note: scree is the loose broken rock on a mountain slope

explanation.surface: A slope of loose stones calls for a fresh fence to hold it back.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen is a partition or shield that separates or protects, so a kind of barrier.

clue.text: There will be a charge in this case

definitions.text: There will be a charge in this case

parts.words: There will be a charge in this case
parts.note: reads like a lawyer's view of a criminal case, but the case is a casing that holds an explosive charge for a gun

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a prosecution; 'charge' is gunpowder and 'case' is its metal or paper shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's ammunition round is a casing packed with propellant, which is the charge.

clue.text: Pay attention to what the Spectator does

definitions.meaning: to observe closely or keep an eye on
a spectator looks on at an event; The Spectator is also a British magazine, adding misdirection

explanation.walkthrough: The capital S hints at The Spectator, a British weekly magazine, but it is just any onlooker.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are about looking: observing closely, and being an onlooker at a show.

clue.text: Type of crime committed by a prisoner?

definitions.text: Type of crime committed by a prisoner?

parts.words: Type of crime committed by a prisoner?
parts.note: a robbery helped by staff is the usual sense, but a prisoner works from within the jail

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means a crime done with help from someone on the staff; the clue takes 'inside' literally as in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime carried out by or with an employee of the victim is called this, and a convict is literally on the inside.

definitions.meaning: a seductive woman, after the ... of Greek myth who lured sailors
a warning device on an ambulance or police car

explanation.definitionFit: The mythical temptresses gave their name to alluring women and later to the loud alarm.

clue.text: Look before you take such a year

definitions.text: Look before you take such a year

parts.words: Look before you take such a year
parts.note: plays on the proverb about looking before jumping and on the calendar year with an extra day

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'Look before you leap' is bent so the jump becomes a kind of year with 29 February.
explanation.definitionFit: A year with an added day in February shares its name with the jump in the proverb.

indicators.note: something that contributed to a word has been put into the middle of it

parts.note: arty means artistic or cultural
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch helped fund a TV channel devoted to the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' looks like a TV station in this surface, but it is a body passage.
explanation.definitionFit: An artery is a main vessel carrying blood, and figuratively a main route or channel.

indicators.note: amazing is read as bewildering, throwing the letters of the panel into a new order

explanation.surface: A brass player astonished the judging panel on a talent show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trumpeter' looks like a musician, but it is an animal that trumpets.
explanation.definitionFit: This animal is famous for its loud trumpeting call through its trunk.

indicators.note: the letters wanted lie inside the word basket

explanation.surface: Asking to see what someone is carrying in their basket.
explanation.definitionFit: To request something is to put a question or demand for it.

clue.text: Draw something of the old school

definitions.meaning: a match ending level
the old school ..., a neckwear badge of a British public school, standing for the old-boy network

explanation.walkthrough: The 'old school tie' is the necktie worn by former pupils of a British private school, a symbol of privileged connections.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn match is a level result, and former pupils wear a striped neckwear badge.

clue.text: Succinct agreement that's put into handbag

definitions.meaning: concise and brief
a pact or treaty
a small case holding face powder and a mirror

explanation.definitionFit: The word means concise, a formal pact, and a small powder case carried in a bag.

definitions.meaning: mock or fake, as in a mock-Latin phrase
a common food fish of northern seas

explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adjective meaning sham, and names a white fish used in fish and chips.

clue.text: This could be raised to part of mouth

definitions.text: This could be raised to part of mouth

parts.words: This could be raised to part of mouth
parts.note: a drinking vessel is lifted to the lips

explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of mouth' stands for the lips; the vessel is raised to them to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cup with a handle is raised to the lips to drink tea or coffee.

definitions.meaning: a stopper that seals a bottle
a port city in the south of Ireland

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it suggests stoppering a bottle of port wine, but the second half is the Irish harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottles are sealed with this bark stopper, and it also names an Irish harbour city.

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds when a race begins
Arkle was a celebrated Irish steeplechaser of the 1960s

explanation.surface: The betting on a fancied horse looks dazzlingly good.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that glitter shine with flashes of light, which is what gems do.

clue.text: Unpleasant period having fibre to eat

parts.note: a rough time is an unpleasant one
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Going through a bad patch and being made to eat bran.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietary fibre from bran, vegetables and grains is the indigestible bulk in food.

indicators.note: a knot is a tangle, so the letters of Gordian are tangled up

explanation.surface: Fascinated by the legendary Gordian knot that Alexander cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Being besotted with someone means being infatuated with and devoted to them.

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of hound, so an exhausted one is a worn-out canine

explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' suggests a fighter, but it is the dog breed, and 'shattered' is British slang for exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: The compound means utterly exhausted, and a worn-out boxer breed fits literally.

definitions.meaning: a key opens a lock, as a tin or bottle ... does
in cricket, one of the two batters who start an innings

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the two openers are the batsmen who go in first.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a tool that unlocks or unseals and a cricketer who starts the innings.

definitions.meaning: in the rhyme 'Tinker, ..., Soldier, Sailor' the second trade comes after tinker
a clothes maker could make you a suit

explanation.walkthrough: The counting rhyme 'Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Sailor' lists trades in order; 'suit' is meant literally as clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The next trade in the counting rhyme is the craftsman who makes men's suits.

definitions.meaning: to suppress or crush, as a rebellion
a fruit cordial diluted with water, in British use

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is also a sweet fruit concentrate diluted with water.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to quell or crush, and is a British fruit cordial.

clue.text: Was a rocker in leather, I gather

indicators.note: I gather is read as I hear, so the word for the leather is taken by its sound

parts.note: suede is a soft napped leather

explanation.surface: A rock fan in a leather jacket, by all accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocker' suggests a leather-clad 1960s British biker, but it means something that rocked to and fro.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rocked moved from side to side, just as a rocking chair does.

parts.note: sin is wickedness or evil
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: Wicked relatives get swallowed up into the household.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts that become fully understood are taken in or absorbed by the mind.

clue.text: Pigment sounds more likely to ooze

indicators.note: sounds says the word for oozier is to be taken by how it is said

parts.note: seepier means more inclined to seep or ooze

explanation.surface: A paint that seems runnier than the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown colouring, originally from cuttlefish ink.

indicators.note: represented is read as presented again in a fresh form, rearranging the letters of nice graph

explanation.surface: A clergyman shows a tidy chart of his parish activities.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar's main duty in the pulpit is delivering sermons to the congregation.

parts.note: le is French for the
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A French tutor was taken in by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone on is to mislead them deliberately, encouraging false hopes.

clue.text: Ocean waves go fast, as before

indicators.note: waves is read as moving in undulations, stirring up the letters of ocean

parts.note: a clock that gains is running fast

explanation.surface: Breakers roll in quickly, just as they did yesterday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go fast' suggests speed, but it is what a clock does when it gains time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something as before means repeating it one more time.
